sections.title: Market snapshot
sections.blurb: Daily prices and rates. Compare these with the headlines; weekly close is the number to weigh.

sections.title: Leading indicators
sections.blurb: Move before the economy does: yield curve, credit, financial conditions, claims, permits, sentiment, liquidity.

sections.title: Coincident indicators
sections.blurb: Describe the economy as it is now: jobs, output, income, spending, real-time recession gauges.

sections.title: Lagging indicators
sections.blurb: Confirm what already happened: unemployment, inflation, loan growth. Useful for the regime, poor for timing.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.src: S&P Dow Jones Indices via FRED (1-day lag)
indicators.desc: US large-cap equities, cap-weighted.

indicators.name: Nasdaq Composite
indicators.src: Nasdaq via FRED (1-day lag)
indicators.desc: Tech-heavy equities; the growth/duration-sensitive end.

indicators.name: Dow Jones Industrial
indicators.src: S&P Dow Jones Indices via FRED (1-day lag)
indicators.desc: 30 large industrials; price-weighted.

indicators.name: 10-year Treasury yield
indicators.src: US Treasury daily par yield curve (treasury.gov, same-day)
indicators.desc: Benchmark long rate; prices mortgages, valuations, and the dollar.

indicators.name: 2-year Treasury yield
indicators.src: US Treasury daily par yield curve (treasury.gov, same-day)
indicators.desc: Where the market expects the policy rate to average over two years.

indicators.name: 4-week T-bill yield
indicators.src: Federal Reserve H.15 via FRED
indicators.desc: What cash earns; the opportunity cost of waiting. Bank-discount basis, so it reads below the investment yield brokers like Fidelity quote.

indicators.name: Fed funds (effective)
indicators.src: Federal Reserve Bank of New York via FRED
indicators.desc: Actual overnight policy rate.

indicators.name: 10-year real yield (TIPS)
indicators.src: US Treasury daily real yield curve (treasury.gov, same-day)
indicators.desc: Inflation-adjusted long rate; the main headwind for gold and long-duration assets.

indicators.name: 10-year breakeven inflation
indicators.src: Federal Reserve H.15 via FRED
indicators.desc: Inflation the bond market is pricing over 10 years.

indicators.name: 30-yr mortgage rate
indicators.src: Freddie Mac PMMS via FRED (weekly, Thursday)
indicators.desc: Housing financing cost; tracks the 10-year plus a spread.

indicators.name: US dollar (broad, trade-weighted)
indicators.src: Federal Reserve Board via FRED (posted weekly, so it runs up to a week behind)
indicators.desc: Dollar vs a broad basket; strength tightens global financial conditions.

indicators.name: WTI crude oil
indicators.src: US EIA via FRED (spot, 1-day lag)
indicators.desc: Energy input cost and an inflation driver.

indicators.name: VIX (S&P 500 implied volatility)
indicators.src: Cboe Global Markets (index publisher)
indicators.desc: Cost of S&P 500 downside protection; the market's fear gauge.

indicators.name: Bitcoin (USD)
indicators.src: Coinbase Exchange daily close, 00:00 UTC (last complete day)
indicators.desc: Trades 24/7. The weekly close is Sunday 00:00 UTC.

indicators.name: Ethereum (USD)
indicators.src: Coinbase Exchange daily close, 00:00 UTC (last complete day)
indicators.desc: Trades 24/7. The weekly close is Sunday 00:00 UTC.

indicators.name: Bitcoin vs 50-week MA, at the last weekly close
indicators.src: Derived from Coinbase weekly closes
indicators.desc: Long-term trend line the market watches; weekly close above or below matters most.

indicators.name: Gold (XAU/USD spot)
indicators.src: Twelve Data XAU/USD spot, last complete day (aggregator; not the LBMA fix)
indicators.desc: Monetary hedge; reacts to real yields and the dollar.

indicators.name: Breadth proxy: equal-weight vs cap-weight (RSP/SPY)
indicators.src: Derived from Twelve Data RSP / SPY closes (ETF prices)
indicators.desc: Rising = the average stock is keeping up; falling = a few mega-caps are carrying the index.

indicators.name: Small caps vs large caps (IWM/SPY)
indicators.src: Derived from Twelve Data IWM / SPY closes (ETF prices)
indicators.desc: Small caps are more rate- and credit-sensitive; a falling ratio is risk-off.

indicators.name: Yield curve: 10-yr minus 3-month
indicators.src: Derived from US Treasury daily par yield curve (10-yr minus 3-month)
indicators.desc: The Fed's preferred curve recession gauge. Below zero = inverted.

indicators.name: Yield curve: 10-yr minus 2-year
indicators.src: Derived from US Treasury daily par yield curve (10-yr minus 2-year)
indicators.desc: Most-quoted curve. Re-steepening after inversion often comes close to the downturn itself.

indicators.name: High-yield credit spread (OAS)
indicators.src: ICE Data Indices via FRED (1-day lag)
indicators.desc: Extra yield junk bonds pay. Lags equity stress by days, leads the real economy by months.

indicators.name: Investment-grade credit spread (OAS)
indicators.src: ICE Data Indices via FRED (1-day lag)
indicators.desc: Spread on high-quality corporates; widens later and more slowly than high-yield.

indicators.name: Financial conditions (Chicago Fed NFCI)
indicators.src: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago via FRED (weekly)
indicators.desc: 105-measure index. Above 0 = tighter than average; below 0 = looser.

indicators.name: Initial jobless claims
indicators.src: US Dept of Labor via FRED (weekly, Thursday)
indicators.desc: First layoff signal; the fastest labor-market data we get.

indicators.name: Building permits (thousands, annualized)
indicators.src: US Census Bureau via FRED
indicators.desc: Housing is rate-sensitive and turns before the rest of the economy.

indicators.name: Consumer sentiment (U. Michigan)
indicators.src: University of Michigan via FRED
indicators.desc: Household mood; noisy, but extremes matter.

indicators.name: M2 money supply, year over year
indicators.src: Federal Reserve Board via FRED
indicators.desc: Broad money growth; the slow-moving liquidity backdrop.

indicators.name: Bank reserves at the Fed
indicators.src: Federal Reserve H.4.1 via FRED (weekly)
indicators.desc: Cash banks hold at the Fed; falling reserves are what stressed money markets in 2019.

indicators.name: Reverse repo facility (overnight)
indicators.src: Federal Reserve Bank of New York via FRED
indicators.desc: Idle cash parked at the Fed; a drawdown releases liquidity into markets.

indicators.name: Net liquidity (Fed assets - Treasury cash - reverse repo)
indicators.src: Derived: Fed H.4.1 total assets, Treasury General Account, NY Fed reverse repo (all via FRED)
indicators.desc: Dollars actually available to the financial system. Widely used, but a convention, not an official statistic.

indicators.name: Policy expectations: 2-yr yield minus Fed funds
indicators.src: Derived: 2-yr yield (US Treasury) minus effective Fed funds rate (NY Fed via FRED)
indicators.desc: Above 0 = market prices hikes; below 0 = prices cuts. Free stand-in for FedWatch odds.

indicators.name: Treasury volatility: 20-day std of 10-yr daily moves (bp)
indicators.src: Derived from US Treasury daily 10-yr yields
indicators.desc: Realized volatility of the 10-yr yield (what already happened). The MOVE index above is the implied counterpart; when they diverge, options traders expect something the recent past does not show.

indicators.name: Nonfarm payrolls, monthly change (thousands)
indicators.src: Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.desc: Jobs added in the month; revisions are large, so trend beats any single print.

indicators.name: Industrial production, year over year
indicators.src: Federal Reserve Board via FRED
indicators.desc: Factory, mining, and utility output.

indicators.name: Real personal income ex-transfers, YoY
indicators.src: Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED
indicators.desc: Earned income after inflation; the cycle-dating committee's own income measure.

indicators.name: Retail sales, year over year (nominal)
indicators.src: US Census Bureau via FRED
indicators.desc: Consumer spending in dollars; compare against inflation to judge real strength.

indicators.name: Sahm rule recession indicator
indicators.src: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis via FRED
indicators.desc: Unemployment 3-mo avg minus its 12-mo low. At 0.50 or above, a recession has historically begun.

indicators.name: GDPNow, current-quarter estimate
indicators.src: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta via FRED
indicators.desc: Model nowcast of real GDP growth, annualized; a model, not a measurement.

indicators.name: Real GDP growth (annualized, latest quarter)
indicators.src: Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED
indicators.desc: The official scorecard, published well after the fact.

indicators.name: Unemployment rate
indicators.src: Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.desc: Peaks after recessions have already started.

indicators.name: Average duration of unemployment (weeks)
indicators.src: Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.desc: How hard it is to get rehired; rises late in a downturn.

indicators.name: CPI, year over year
indicators.src: Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.desc: Headline consumer inflation.

indicators.name: Core CPI, year over year
indicators.src: Bureau of Labor Statistics via FRED
indicators.desc: Inflation excluding food and energy.

indicators.name: Core PCE, year over year
indicators.src: Bureau of Economic Analysis via FRED
indicators.desc: The Fed's inflation target measure.

indicators.name: Commercial & industrial loans, year over year
indicators.src: Federal Reserve H.8 via FRED (weekly)
indicators.desc: Business borrowing; lags the cycle, and a contraction confirms a slowdown.
